data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from OAR)

# OAR requested:
#   -q production
#   -p gpu_model!='NO'
#   -p cluster='grele'
#   -l host=1/gpu=1/core=2,walltime=01:00:00
#   -O ./OUT/oar_job.%jobid%.output
#   -E ./OUT/oar_job.%jobid%.error

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  -c 2 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=1h \
  --queue=production \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p ./OUT

# Approximate OAR %jobid% using Flux job id.
exec >"./OUT/oar_job.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.output" 2>"./OUT/oar_job.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.error"

# NOTE: OAR placement/property constraints (-p gpu_model!=\x27NO\x27 and -p cluster=\x27grele\x27)
# have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: you may be scheduled on nodes outside the intended cluster or without the desired GPU
# characteristics, which can change performance or even break GPU-dependent code.

# This is to activate a python environment with conda
source ~/.bashrc
conda activate se

# Set variables
SEGMENT="$1"
CKPT_PATH="../../pretrained_models/A-VAE/A-VAE.pt"
ALGO_TYPE="peem"
DATA_DIR="/srv/storage/talc@storage4.nancy.grid5000.fr/multispeech/corpus/audio_visual/TCD-TIMIT/test_data_NTCD/test_data_5.pkl"
SAVE_ROOT="./results/"

# Run command
python SE_evaluation.py \
    --segment "$SEGMENT" \
    --ckpt_path "$CKPT_PATH" \
    --algo_type "$ALGO_TYPE" \
    --data_dir "$DATA_DIR" \
    --save_root "$SAVE_ROOT"
'
"
}
